name: KISS FFT
reason: The SourceForge page has no benchmark numbers and no speed claim against FFTPACK or any other library (description: 'The FFT library to Keep It Simple, Stupid'; last update 2018-10-16; states that development moved to https://github.com/mborgerding/kissfft). Same project as the separate kissfft lead from the same list, so see that entry for the numbers that exist (all of which show it slower than FFTW, FFTPACK-derived pocketfft and others). The guessed baseline FFTPACK has no kissfft-wins row anywhere reachable except tiny sizes (n of 8 or less) in the pffft_benchmarks table.

name: kissfft
listed_description: A Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) library that tries to Keep it Simple, Stupid.
reason: Nobody claims it is faster than a named baseline; every number found shows it slower. README BACKGROUND: 'FFT_BRANDX is roughly twice as fast as KISS FFT in default mode' (BRANDX unnamed, implied FFTW), 'DO NOT: use Kiss if you need the Fastest Fourier Transform in the World'; its PERFORMANCE section is one old timing (Athlon XP 2100+, gcc 2.96, float: 10000 1024-pt complex FFTs in 0.63 s) compared only with md5sum. Third-party numbers, flagged not-faster if the orchestrator wants a record: project-gemmi/benchmarking-fft (i7-5600U, GCC 8 -O3, float, 1D complex-to-complex n=512: kissfft 6553 ns vs fftw3 measured 588 ns, mufft 719 ns, pffft 1255 ns, and with SIMD disabled pocketfft 4009 ns, meow_fft 4342 ns; 3D 416x256x416: kissfft 4235 ms vs fftw3 measured 727 ms, pocketfft 939 ms); hayguen/pffft_benchmarks, i7-8550U gcc 9.3.0 single-precision complex n=1024: Kiss 5831 MFLOPS vs FFTPack 8579, FFTW F(auto) 55947 (Kiss beats FFTPack only at n of 8 or less: n=2 1154 vs 497, n=4 3424 vs 1322, n=8 2436 vs 1848 MFLOPS, and that table uses hayguen's fork of kissfft). Pages opened: https://github.com/mborgerding/kissfft, https://github.com/project-gemmi/benchmarking-fft, https://github.com/hayguen/pffft_benchmarks. Its value is size and simplicity (core about 500 lines, fixed-point support), not speed.

name: Kratos
listed_description: framework for building parallel, multi-disciplinary simulation software, aiming at modularity, extensibility, and high performance.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. README only says 'aiming at ... high performance' and lists Google Benchmark among dependencies (own micro-benchmarks, no published results). The wiki's only benchmarking page, 'Basic DEM Benchmarking', is nine validation tests (elastic and oblique impacts, restitution) checked against a 2011 code-verification paper, with no timings or other codes. WebSearch for Kratos against FEniCS, deal.II, Abaqus, Bullet or ODE found no Kratos timing comparison. The guessed category blas-lapack and baselines ODE or Bullet are wrong: Kratos is a finite-element and multiphysics framework (fluid, structure, DEM) whose natural baselines would be FEniCS, deal.II or MOOSE; its published papers were not reachable (arXiv and journal sites blocked).

name: LAMMPS
listed_description: A classical molecular dynamics code with a focus on materials modeling. It's an acronym for Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator.
reason: No number against GROMACS, NAMD or OpenMM that shows LAMMPS faster, and no cross-code number at all on reachable pages. The repo's doc/src/Speed_bench.rst and bench/README describe only LAMMPS's own five standard problems (LJ, Chain, EAM, Chute, Rhodo, 32,000 atoms, 100 steps) and send readers to www.lammps.org/bench.html (EGRESS_BLOCKED, as were matsci.org and arXiv). NgFEP/NgFEP-assessment (GROMACS 23.3, NAMD 3, OpenMM 8.1, AMBER 22 ns/day on 12 GPUs) and HECBioSim/hpcbench (tooling only, no published numbers) do not include a LAMMPS result. Search-summary hints only, unopened and unverified: an old forum comparison said GROMACS was about 2x faster than LAMMPS for 2048 SPC/E waters on a Core 2 Quad; arXiv 1401.4350 and 1009.4330 report HOOMD-blue about 2x faster than LAMMPS-GPU. The record for GROMACS in this run carries the independent GROMACS-vs-NAMD-vs-OpenMM numbers. Retry LAMMPS in an environment with arXiv access (arXiv 2506.15585 compares GROMACS, NAMD and LAMMPS in ns/day on several HPC systems). The guessed category geometry-spatial fits only loosely; no wave 8 category covers molecular dynamics.

name: libsvm
listed_description: A simple, easy-to-use, efficient library for Support Vector Machines.
reason: The repo has no benchmark numbers: README (file name README, not README.md) and FAQ.html contain no comparison with any other library; the only speed statements are internal (sparse format makes kernel evaluation slower so training can take 'at least twice or three times' as long as dense; the Java port is 'still slower' than C++). The guessed baselines tensorflow and pytorch are wrong: LIBSVM is a kernel-SVM solver and is itself the usual baseline that ThunderSVM, liquidSVM and other SVM tools compare against (scikit-learn's SVC wraps it). The project homepage www.csie.ntu.edu.tw/~cjlin/libsvm and PMC were EGRESS_BLOCKED. A WebSearch result summary mentioned a liquidSVM paper table (arXiv 1702.06899, not opened, unverified) with COD-RNA n=1000 training times LIBSVM 34.5 s vs SVMlight 665.6 s, and another snippet said SVMlight is faster on sparse data; treat as a lead for an environment with arXiv access, not as evidence.
